messages.onboarding.intro: Sign in once with your {{.Tenant.Name}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} details. p.stonn keeps an encrypted session so it can update your permit for you.
messages.onboarding.email_pinned: Your {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account must use this same email. You can’t change it here.
messages.onboarding.reset_beside: If you have an {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account but do not know the password, you can {{slot "reset"}}reset it at the council{{endslot}}, then come back and link here.
messages.onboarding.register_beside: If you have never used {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}}, you will need to {{slot "register"}}create an account at the council{{endslot}} first. p.stonn can only link to an account you already hold.
messages.onboarding.saved_password_why: p.stonn stores your password encrypted and uses it only to sign back in when the council ends the session, which the council does whenever you sign in to the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} yourself.
messages.onboarding.rejected_lead: p.stonn tried to sign in with {{slot "b"}}{{.User.Email}}{{endslot}}. Either the password is not the one the council holds, or your {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account uses a different email.
messages.onboarding.rejected_reset: {{slot "b"}}If you have forgotten your council password, or have never set one,{{endslot}} you can {{slot "reset"}}reset it at the council{{endslot}}, then come back and link your account here. This is the most common fix.
messages.onboarding.rejected_try_portal: If you are unsure which applies, try your details at the council’s own {{slot "portal"}}{{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}{{endslot}} first.
messages.onboarding.paused_password: If the email is correct, double-check the password: try it at the council’s own {{slot "portal"}}{{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}{{endslot}}, and if it fails there too, {{slot "reset"}}reset it at the council{{endslot}}.
messages.onboarding.picker_error: If p.stonn still cannot load your permits, check that the council’s own {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} is working.
messages.onboarding.picker_none: If you expected a visitor permit here, check it on the council’s own {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}: it may have expired, or be held by another resident at your address. It’s also possible the council changed something on its side that p.stonn doesn’t recognise yet.
messages.onboarding.picker_apply: Apply for a visitor permit on the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} first, then come back and the permit will appear here.
messages.settings.password_saved: Your password is saved (encrypted) so p.stonn can sign back in on its own if the council ends your session. Signing in to the {{.Tenant.Short}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} yourself still signs p.stonn out until it next reconnects.
messages.settings.password_not_saved: Your password isn’t saved. If the council ends your session, including when you sign in to the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} yourself, you’ll need to link your account again by hand. To turn this on, unlink and link again with “Save my password” ticked.
messages.terms.next_step: Next you’ll connect your council account, which takes your {{slot "b"}}{{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} password{{endslot}}. If you’re not sure you have one, {{slot "reset"}}reset it at the council{{endslot}} while you’re here.
messages.guest.credit: The resident manages this permit with {{slot "home"}}p.stonn{{endslot}}, which is free for {{.Tenant.Name}} residents.
messages.guest.own_household: If your own household has a visitor permit, p.stonn is free for {{.Tenant.Name}} residents.
messages.guests.poster_foot: This poster was made with p.stonn, which is unofficial and not run by the {{.Tenant.Name}}.
messages.share.intro: p.stonn is free for any {{.Tenant.Short}} household with a visitor parking permit. If someone you know is still changing the number plate by hand, here’s how to send it their way.
messages.share.poster_lead: Your {{.Tenant.Short}} visitor parking permit, on a schedule.
messages.share.poster_note: You can set a weekly roster for regular visitors and make bookings for everyone else. Your visitors can put their own rego on with a guest pass or visitor QR. p.stonn is free for {{.Tenant.Name}} residents.
messages.public.hero_note: p.stonn is free for {{.Tenant.Name}} residents ({{.Tenant.SuburbList}}). You sign in with a one-time code sent to your email.
messages.public.need_account: You’ll need an existing {{.Tenant.Name}} {{slot "b"}}{{.Tenant.Terms.portal}}{{endslot}} account with a visitor permit on it. Sign in here with {{slot "b"}}the same email address your {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account uses{{endslot}}, because p.stonn can only connect to the council account that matches. It schedules a permit you already hold and can’t apply for one. {{slot "how"}}What you need →{{endslot}}
messages.public.step_link: Sign in with your {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} email, then connect with your council password.
messages.public.other_area: p.stonn is built to schedule any council that runs this kind of online visitor-permit system, not just {{.Tenant.Name}}. The groundwork for new areas is already in place. Adding one takes someone local with a permit account to help work out how their council’s site behaves. If that’s your council and you’d like to help bring it here, {{slot "contact"}}get in touch{{endslot}}. A test account is all it takes to get started.
messages.public.disclaimer: p.stonn is an unofficial app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the {{.Tenant.Name}}. You remain responsible for your permit and any fines. {{slot "security"}}Security & data{{endslot}}
messages.public.about_unofficial: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling your {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the council. See {{slot "how"}}what p.stonn can do{{endslot}}.
messages.public.faq_unofficial: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling your {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit. It is not affiliated with the council. See {{slot "how"}}what p.stonn can do{{endslot}}.
messages.public.history: {{.Tenant.Short}} Council changed how resident and visitor parking permits work in 2026. Paper visitor permits have been phased out in favour of a digital system. The digital permit requires you to enter vehicle registration numbers into the council’s online system, and parking officers check it as they patrol the streets.
messages.public.attempt: p.stonn is an attempt to make that easier. Once you have a permit set up with {{.Tenant.Terms.parking_brand}}, you can use it to set which rego is on the permit each day of the week, add one-off bookings, and hand a visitor a QR link that puts their rego on when they arrive.
messages.public.before_intro: p.stonn does not replace the council's system. It works on top of a permit you already hold, so you need a {{.Tenant.Name}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account with at least one visitor permit first.
messages.public.council_pages: The council’s own pages: {{slot "apply"}}visitor parking permits{{endslot}} and {{slot "faq"}}parking permit FAQs{{endslot}}.
messages.public.faq_more: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool and is not affiliated with the {{.Tenant.Name}}. {{T "public.council_pages" .}} See also {{slot "how"}}what p.stonn can do{{endslot}} and the {{slot "faq_page"}}FAQ{{endslot}}.
messages.capacity.full: p.stonn is full at the moment. One person runs it for a small number of {{.Tenant.Short}} households, and taking on more right now would make it slower and less reliable for everyone already using it. Please try again in a while, or get in touch and we’ll let you know when there’s room.
messages.picker.session_rejected: The council accepted your password, so the sign-in itself worked. But when p.stonn then asked the council for your permit list, the council turned the request away. That usually means the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account isn’t fully set up yet, for example because it was only just created or doesn’t have a permit on it. Entering your password here again won’t change this. Please sign in at the council’s own site ({{.Tenant.PortalHost}}) and check your visitor permit appears there, then come back and link again. If the permit is there and this keeps happening, please get in touch via the contact form.
messages.schedule.added_expired: You added that permit, but it is no longer active at the council, so p.stonn will not apply anything to it. It’s under “Permits no longer active” below. Renew it on the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}, then copy its schedule onto the new permit when it appears here.
messages.mail.provenance: You received this at {{.To}} because {{.Reason}}. p.stonn is a free, unofficial scheduler for {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permits.
messages.mail.footer_affiliation: p.stonn is not affiliated with the {{.Tenant.Name}}.
messages.mail.referral_line: If you know another {{.Tenant.Short}} household with a visitor permit, you are welcome to send them to p.stonn.org.
messages.mail.invite_lead: {{.Owner}} has given you shared access to their p.stonn account, which schedules a {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit.
messages.mail.invite_reminder_lead: {{.Owner}} gave you shared access to their p.stonn account a few days ago, which schedules a {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit. The invitation is still waiting for you to accept it.
messages.mail.invite_unaccepted_lead: You invited {{.Member}} to share your p.stonn account, and they have not accepted it yet. Until they do, they cannot see or change your {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor permit.
messages.mail.nudge_connect: Linking takes one sign-in with your {{.Tenant.Name}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} details. Most people who get stuck have run into one of three things.
messages.mail.nudge_password: 1. If you have forgotten your {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} password, or have never set one, the council can reset it for you.
messages.mail.nudge_email: 2. p.stonn can only link to the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account registered under the address you signed up with ({{.To}}). If your council account uses a different email, sign in to p.stonn with that address instead.
messages.mail.nudge_apply: If you do not have an {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} account or a visitor permit yet, please apply for a visitor permit on the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}} first, then come back.
messages.mail.portal_nudge_lead: Someone on your account put a new number plate on your visitor permit using the {{.Tenant.Name}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} site: {{.Plate}}
messages.mail.portal_nudge_fine: Changing number plates on the {{.Tenant.Name}} website works just fine with p.stonn. There is also an easier way.
messages.mail.guest_lead: This link from {{.Owner}} lets you put a rego on their {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit ({{.Label}}).
messages.mail.guest_promo: If you have a visitor permit of your own, p.stonn is free for {{.Tenant.Name}} residents at p.stonn.org.
messages.mail.fortnight_line: If p.stonn has been handy, you might know someone else in {{.Tenant.Short}} with a visitor permit who’d get some use out of it too.
messages.mail.referral_lead: {{.Sender}} uses p.stonn to look after their {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit, and thought it might be useful for you too.
messages.mail.referral_body: p.stonn changes the rego on your visitor permit for you, with a weekly roster for regulars, one-off bookings for everyone else, and a guest pass or QR code your visitors can use themselves. It’s free for {{.Tenant.Short}} residents.
messages.mail.renewal_body:
Hi,

Your visitor-permit scheduler is still running and updating your permit automatically.

We haven’t seen you in p.stonn for a while, so this is a check that you still want it running. If you do nothing, it will stop on {{.When}} and you’ll need to link your council account again.

Signing in to p.stonn does the same thing as clicking below.

Confirm and keep it running (one click):
{{.URL}}

If you no longer want the service, you can ignore this email and it will stop on its own.

-- p.stonn
messages.seo.landing_title: {{.Tenant.Short}} visitor parking permits, on a schedule — p.stonn
messages.seo.landing_desc: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling the rego on your {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit, with a weekly roster, a guest pass for family, or a QR code for tradies.
messages.seo.how_title: What p.stonn can do with your {{.Tenant.Short}} visitor permit
messages.seo.how_desc: Connect your {{.Tenant.Short}} {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} login once, and p.stonn puts the right rego on your visitor permit on your schedule, with one-off bookings, visitor QR codes, a printed QR and guest passes.
messages.seo.security_desc: This page explains what p.stonn encrypts, how long it keeps your data, what a breach could reach and how to delete everything. p.stonn is a free, unofficial {{.Tenant.Short}} parking tool.
messages.seo.contact_desc: If you have questions about p.stonn, the free scheduler for {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permits, get in touch.
messages.seo.faq_desc: These answers cover scheduling your {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit with p.stonn, including recurring visitors, sharing with family, cost and safety.
messages.faq.safe_q: Is it safe to give p.stonn my {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} login?
messages.faq.which_council_a: p.stonn covers the {{.Tenant.Name}}’s visitor parking permits (the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal}} system) in {{.Tenant.SuburbList}}. It does not support other councils yet.
messages.guide.signin_step: Sign in at {{slot "portal"}}{{.Tenant.PortalHost}}{{endslot}}. {{slot "register"}}Register{{endslot}} first if you haven’t, or {{slot "reset"}}reset your password{{endslot}} if you’ve never used it.
messages.guide.change_title: How do I change the car on my {{.Tenant.Short}} visitor permit? — p.stonn
messages.guide.change_desc: This guide explains how to change the rego on a {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permit on the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}, and how to stop doing it by hand.
messages.guide.change_h1: How do I change the car on my {{.Tenant.Short}} visitor permit?
messages.guide.change_para: On the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}, sign in, choose Update Vehicle on the permit, enter the new number plate and save. You have to do this before each visitor parks.
messages.guide.change_note: You can also ring the council on {{.Tenant.Phone}} to change the rego.
messages.guide.carer_title: Visitor parking for a cleaner, nanny or carer in {{.Tenant.Short}} — p.stonn
messages.guide.carer_desc: A {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor permit covers one rego at a time. This guide explains how to handle a cleaner, nanny or carer who comes every week without changing the number plate by hand.
messages.guide.carer_h1: Visitor parking for a cleaner, nanny or carer in {{.Tenant.Short}}
messages.guide.carer_note: Carer arrangements can also qualify for a physical permit under the council’s {{slot "apply"}}exceptional circumstances{{endslot}} provision, so it is worth asking the council if the online system doesn’t suit your household.
messages.guide.paper_title: Do visitors need a paper permit in {{.Tenant.Short}}? — p.stonn
messages.guide.paper_desc: {{.Tenant.Name}} visitor parking permits are digital by default, so there is nothing to display, but the number plate has to be right before each visitor parks. This guide explains what that means in practice.
messages.guide.paper_h1: Do visitors need a paper permit in {{.Tenant.Short}}?
messages.guide.login_title: {{.Tenant.Short}} parking permit login: where to sign in — p.stonn
messages.guide.login_desc: The {{.Tenant.Name}}’s parking permit login is its {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}. This guide covers what to sign in with, how to reset the password, what to do if you have never registered, and how to stop signing in at all.
messages.guide.login_h1: Where do I log in to my {{.Tenant.Short}} parking permit?
messages.guide.login_para1: {{.Tenant.Short}} parking permits live on the council’s {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}, {{.Tenant.PortalHost}}.{{if .Tenant.Terms.manage_button}} The council’s own website reaches it through the ‘{{.Tenant.Terms.manage_button}}’ button on its parking permits page{{if .Tenant.Terms.app}}, and the {{.Tenant.Terms.app}} through its ‘Parking permits’ tile. All three{{else}}. Both{{end}} open the same login screen.{{end}}
messages.guide.login_para2: You sign in with the email address you registered with and a password of at least fifteen characters. There is no separate username; where the site asks for one, it means your email.
messages.guide.login_step_open: Open {{slot "portal"}}the {{.Tenant.Terms.portal_site}}{{endslot}} and enter your email and password.
messages.guide.login_step_reset: If you have forgotten the password, choose {{slot "reset"}}Forgot your password?{{endslot}} The username it asks for is your email address, and the reset link arrives by email.
messages.guide.login_step_register: If you have never registered, choose {{slot "register"}}Register as a new user{{endslot}}. The account comes first and you apply for permits from inside it; a permit from the paper days does not come with a login.
messages.guide.login_step_permits: Once you are in, your permits are listed under Current Permits. {{slot "b"}}Update Vehicle{{endslot}} on the {{.Tenant.Terms.permit}} is where a visitor’s number plate goes.
messages.guide.login_note: If the site will not let you in, the council’s Customer Service team on {{.Tenant.Phone}} can help during business hours, and can put a visitor’s rego on your permit over the phone.
messages.guide.paper_note: For a physical permit, see {{slot "apply"}}the council’s visitor-permit page{{endslot}} for the exceptional-circumstances application, or ring {{.Tenant.Phone}}.
messages.picker.connect_first: Connect your {{.Tenant.Name}} account to add a permit from there.
messages.picker.reconnecting: Your council sign-in had expired, so p.stonn is signing back in with your saved password. This page refreshes itself, and your permits should appear in a few seconds.
